title: Latency-first KV-aware batch formation for streaming responses
creator: Ana Rodriguez
description: Goal: implement a batch formation policy optimized for low tail latency in streaming chat completions while minimizing GPU KV cache churn and peak memory usage. This ticket covers the design and implementation of a "latency-first, KV-aware" batcher that prioritizes on-deck requests close to emission deadlines, coalesces compatible prefix KV shards, and performs adaptive GPU memory compaction between bursts. The outcome should reduce 95th/99th percentile end-to-end token latency for streaming chat workloads by at least 20% on mixed short/long session traffic without increasing average GPU memory usage by more than 10%.
acceptance_criteria: New batcher can be toggled via runtime feature flag and has unit + integration tests
95th percentile token emission latency reduced >= 20% on benchmark mixed-chat workload compared to current production batcher
GPU peak memory increase <= 10% on same benchmark workload
KV cache hit-rate does not regress more than 2 percentage points; when beneficial, show improved reuse through prefix coalescing
No client-facing ordering regressions for streaming chunks; all existing streaming semantics preserved
Rollout playbook documented and monitored dashboards created
technical_notes: Batch formation policy: compute a per-request urgency score = min(time-to-deadline, tail-safety-margin) - estimated-queueing-delay; prioritize higher urgency while allowing small opportunistic merges of lower-urgency requests up to a max_coalesce_window (config: 15ms by default)

KV awareness: track prefix shard fingerprints and group requests that will reuse identical KV slices to avoid redundant KV materialization on GPU; maintain an LRU of 'warm shards' to prefer grouping when beneficial
GPU memory compaction: after each emission burst, trigger async slab compaction and deferred eviction of cold KV slices; ensure compaction budgeted under background IO to avoid blocking inferences
Pre-allocated KV slices: introduce per-device pre-allocated KV buffers with fast-slice allocator to reduce allocation overhead for short sessions (configurable pool size)
Backpressure: expose backpressure signal when batch queue grows beyond token-cost-based threshold; upstream caller path will adapt to avoid queue pile-up
Streaming tail-chunk policy: for partial-streamed responses, send small low-latency chunks for the first N tokens, then opportunistically aggregate subsequent tokens if batch formation allows
Trade-offs: aggressive coalescing reduces compute overhead but can increase tail latency for urgent requests; policy tunables (max_coalesce_window, urgency_weight) allow balancing
Compatibility: keep existing metrics (per-token-latency, batch-size, kv_materializations) and add new ones (urgency_score_distribution, prefix_coalesce_rate, compaction_time_ms)
rollout_plan: Feature-flag behind runtime flag 'latency_first_batcher' and gated to 5% of traffic in canary cluster
Stage 1 (Canary): enable on non-critical tenants + internal benchmark traffic, run for 48h, validate metrics
Stage 2 (Ramp): 25% traffic for 72h, compare A/B against baseline, watch 95/99p latencies and memory
Stage 3 (Full): Gradual rollout to 100% with stepdowns if 99p latency regresses or GPU OOMs observed
Rollback: revert flag and trigger immediate passive eviction of pre-allocated KV slices
monitoring_and_metrics: prefix_coalesce_rate (ratio of batches with >1 request sharing KV shard)
test_plan: Unit tests for urgency scoring and batch eligibility logic
Integration test: synthetic mixed-chat load generator (short: 8-16 tokens; long: 256+ tokens) to validate latency and memory behavior in CI
Stress test: ramp to peak QPS with randomized prefix reuse patterns to validate KV shard grouping and compaction stability
Chaos test: simulate device GC/eviction delays and verify backpressure and safe degradation
Perf regression job added to nightly benchmarking suite comparing baseline vs latency-first batcher
